sources.entry: Tura - Tura is a local, open-source coding agent for developers who are tired of vague skill claims, token-saving extensions with no evidence, and agents that change a repository before understanding it. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/Tura-AI/tura) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.name: Tura
summary.one_liner: Tura is a local, open-source coding agent, with an evaluation and optimization platform that benchmarks agent strategies on long-horizon workflows and reports cost and completed outcomes.
use_cases: benchmark agent strategies on real workflows
reduce LLM turns and token spend for coding agents
evaluate agent success rate and runtime cost
connect internal tools and APIs to agents with permissions
automatically optimize prompts and workflows from eval results
summary.what_it_does: The page describes Tura as a local, open-source coding agent and an evaluation platform for agent workflows. It reports benchmark results across 558 published sessions (20 DeepSWE tasks, 5 rewrite tasks, and 2 design tasks), averaging 36.4 agent turns per session. On the tested long-horizon benchmark, it claims an 83.1% reduction in LLM turns and token usage with a 16.7% performance improvement. Tura also offers governed tool calling for internal APIs and permission systems, and CLI macros and decision trees that group patching, compiling, validation and log inspection into fewer model turns. The install command shown is npm install tura-ai.
notable: Reports completed outcomes alongside resource usage (turns and tokens) for each comparison
Published evidence covering 558 sessions across DeepSWE, rewrite and design tasks
CLI macros and decision trees to reduce model turns
Open-source, listed in awesome-mac under AI Tools
caveats: Headline 80%+ savings and 83.1% turn/token reduction are self-reported vendor benchmark figures, on a limited task set (20 DeepSWE, 5 rewrite, 2 design tasks)
Design audits are reported separately from the other results
Pricing not stated on the page
